title: Признание Насте и пленник в холодильнике  (Confessing to Nastya and the Captive in the Fridge)

segments.t: In the kitchen, Max finally admits to a horrified Nastya that the morning rolls her vegetarian guest loved were actually stuffed with meat. Meanwhile, Kristina storms into the restaurant after waiting an hour for her contact, who answers his phone from inside the walk-in fridge.
Ох и вонь у нас там, ребята.
Там и воняет, и холод потом.
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
'What is in there?' Max raises the pitch on 'such a' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Dmitry answers right away.
'What do you mean, meat?' The grammar packs 'how' and 'meat' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Maksim, did you put meat in his food?' Max addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'meat'.
'He is happy with it, do not get upset.' Dmitry anchors the line on 'yes', while 'be upset' completes the thought. Max answers right away.
'How could you do that?' Max addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'could'.
'If nothing happens...' Dmitry anchors the line on 'if', while 'nothing' completes the thought.
'I have been waiting for you for an hour already.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'I' and finishing on 'I'm waiting'. Dmitry answers right away.
'Where have you been wandering?' Dmitry raises the pitch on 'can walk' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question.
'I am sitting inside the walk-in fridge.' The grammar packs 'I' and 'am sitting' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Ох и вонь у нас там, ребята.
'Oh, it really stinks in there, guys.' Russian expresses 'having' with the preposition 'by' plus the genitive pronoun and 'kids'. Max answers right away.
Там и воняет, и холод потом.
'First it stinks in there, and then it is freezing cold.' Max brings out the contrast between 'there' and 'both' in a few short words.
'So who is she?' Dmitry brings out the contrast between 'come on' and 'both' in a few short words.
'Oh, let us say so.' Notice how Russian expresses 'oh' and 'to allow' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Alright, let's hear the whole conversation once more from start to finish.
Ох и вонь у нас там, ребята.
Там и воняет, и холод потом.

When you watch Scene 17 of Episode 13, listen out for the exchange around confessing to nastya and the captive in the fridge — you will recognize every Russian phrase right away. See you in the next scene.
